## Problem
In run `execute-epic-ticket-576-loop-18`, merge-down's publish step pushed PR #732's fix commit with `git push --force-with-lease=…:c24ee7d origin c20fa73:refs/heads/epic-576/726-…`. GitHub rejected it with `remote: fatal error in commit_refs_rules` / `! [remote rejected] … (fatal error in commit_refs_rules)`. The run blocked at publish and the loop stopped. The identical push, run by hand a few minutes later, succeeded (fast-forward c24ee7d..c20fa73), and githubstatus.com showed no incident for Git operations.

## Proposal
In the publish step, treat a `[remote rejected]` caused by a server-side error (for example `fatal error in commit_refs_rules`, `internal server error`, or a 5xx) as transient. Re-read the remote tip; if it still equals the lease, retry the same push a bounded number of times with backoff before blocking. Lease mismatches and policy rejections (protected branch, required signatures) still block at once.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A push rejected with a transient server error is retried, with the lease re-checked first, and succeeds when the retry does.
- [ ] Lease mismatches and policy rejections still block without a retry.
- [ ] A step test covers both cases with a fake `git` that fails the first push.

_Part of #594. Found during the #576 burndown (PR #732)._

## What to build

A developer can get an entry's SEO values and put them in the page's `<head>` with one call, or opt in to having that done for template-rendered entries.

`$entry->seo()` returns the title, description, canonical URL and Open Graph values. A blueprint maps which fields feed them, falling back to `title` and the first paragraph of the body. `content_seo($entry)` pushes them into `viewMeta`. Automatic injection sits behind `Config\Content::$autoSeo`, which is off by default, in line with ADR 0002: nothing is added to a response silently.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `$entry->seo()` returns values from the fields the blueprint maps.
- [ ] With no mapping, the title comes from `title` and the description from the first paragraph of the body, as plain text.
- [ ] The canonical URL uses the entry's computed URI.
- [ ] `content_seo($entry)` makes the values appear in the rendered `<head>`, with values escaped.
- [ ] With `$autoSeo` off (the default), a template-rendered entry gets no added tags.
- [ ] With `$autoSeo` on, a template-rendered entry gets them. A collection that hands off to a controller stays the developer's to call.
- [ ] Works for an entry reached through a template, a controller, or a hand-written route using `findByUri()`.
- [ ] Docs and changelog entry.

Workarounds in the build, CI and release setup, why they exist, and when they can go. Each one has a comment next to it in the repository.

### release-plz's PR job checks out without submodules
- **Where:** `.github/workflows/release.yml`, job `release-plz-pr`.
- **Why:** to write the changelog, release-plz checks out older commits, and the history goes back to when CMSIS-NN and ESP-NN were vendored files; git refuses to restore them over checked-out submodules (`untracked working tree files would be overwritten by checkout`). The same happens with `git rebase` across that transition.
- **Remove:** now that v0.1.0 is tagged, add `submodules: recursive` back (release-plz only walks the commits after the last release tag).

### `mise run package` clears Cargo's extracted registry sources
- **Where:** `mise.toml`, task `package` (`rm -rf ... registry/src/-*/nanoglia-*`, `MBX_BUILD_SCRIPT_EXECUTION=false`).
- **Why:** `cargo package --workspace` verifies each crate against the others through a temporary registry with the same path and versions on every run, and never re-extracts a registry package it has seen. The CI cache kept an old `nanoglia-cmsis-nn 0.1.0` extraction, so `nanoglia-esp-nn` was verified against sources without the `kernels` module (Release workflow failure). Same issue and fix as lvgl_rust_sys.
- **Remove:** never, as long as unpublished versions are packaged repeatedly; harmless.

### crates.io limits the publication of new crates
- **What happened:** publishing v0.1.0 stopped after 5 new crates with `429 Too Many Requests: You have published too many new crates in a short period of time`; the failed `release-plz-release` job was re-run later (`gh run rerun <id> --failed`), and release-plz published only the missing crates.
- **Next time:** only new crate names are limited; new versions of existing crates are not. A new crate in the workspace may need a re-run.

### Release PRs do not trigger CI
- **Why:** release-plz opens its PR with the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub does not start workflows for it; with the branch protection of `main` (required checks), the release PR cannot be merged without an admin bypass.
- **Fix:** set the `RELEASE_PLZ_TOKEN` secret (a personal token with `contents` and `pull-requests` write), already used by `release.yml` when present.

### ESP32-S3 builds bypass mise's Cargo wrapper
- **Where:** `mise.toml`, task `cross-esp32s3` (`RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=esp`, `mbx build ... -Zbuild-std=core`).
- **Why:** mise's `cargo` wrapper probes the workspace with the stable toolchain and fails on `-Z` flags; the Xtensa target needs the `esp` toolchain from espup and `build-std`. `CC` points at `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-gcc` because the generic `xtensa-esp-elf-gcc` rejects the PIE instructions.
- **Remove:** when the Xtensa target is in upstream Rust, or mise's wrapper handles nightly flags.

### Targets with a dot in their name use generic C variables
- **Where:** `mise.toml` (`ARM_NEWLIB_FLAGS`, `TARGET_CC`/`TARGET_CFLAGS` in `cross-arm`).
- **Why:** `CFLAGS_thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf` & co. do not survive mbx's build-script wrapper, a POSIX `sh` script (dash drops such variable names).

### wasm32-unknown-unknown takes C headers from the wasi-sdk sysroot
- **Where:** `mise.toml`, task `cross-wasm32`; `documentation/how-to-guides/run-in-the-browser.md`.
- **Why:** CMSIS-NN and ESP-NN include `string.h`/`stdint.h`, which `wasm32-unknown-unknown` has no sysroot for; only the declarations are needed (`memcpy` & co. come from Rust's `compiler_builtins`).

### Dependabot ignores torch in the oracle project
- **Where:** `.github/dependabot.yml`, uv entry.
- **Why:** `litert-torch` pins `torch < 2.15`; updating torch alone makes the lockfile unsolvable.
- **Remove:** never needed; torch moves with litert-torch.

### The PyTorch export only runs in CI
- **Where:** `tools/oracle/pytorch_export.py`, mise task `pytorch-export`, CI job "PyTorch export (litert-torch, int8)".
- **Why:** `litert-converter` (needed by litert-torch) only ships x86_64 Linux and macOS arm64 wheels; it cannot run on the aarch64 Linux development VM.

### Transient GitHub push errors
- Pushes sometimes failed with `fatal error in commit_refs_rules` or `Internal Server Error` while GitHub's status page reported no incident; retrying succeeded. Not a repository problem.
title: Workarounds: build, CI and release tooling

Kind: plumbing

A run's result is recorded with a single push, so one failure from GitHub at the end of a run throws away the whole run.

On 2026-11-04 at 10:20:08 UTC, #445's draft finished after about 16 minutes. The watcher saved the result as a local commit, and `Clone.Finish` in `internal/factory/runs.go` pushed it to `refs/invariant/runs/445/draft-6627806027`. GitHub answered `500 Internal Server Error`, so the step returned the error, and the result commit never left the watcher's clone. The next holder found the run recorded with no result, and posted that the draft's agent run had stopped partway. The draft has to run again. In the same hour, pushes to this repository failed with 500s and with `fatal error in commit_refs_rules` at 09:41, 09:46, from 10:00 to 10:03, and at 10:20 and 10:21. The pushes in between succeeded. A build's result is recorded the same way, so a two-hour build can be lost at its last step.

`Finish` should get a result through GitHub's failures before giving up:

- After a failed push, it reads the run's ref. If the ref already holds the result, the push landed, and `Finish` succeeds.
- If the ref still holds the run's record and the failure was GitHub failing rather than refusing, `Finish` tries again after waits of 15, 30, 60 and 120 seconds. Failing means a 5xx, `fatal error in commit_refs_rules`, a timeout or a dropped connection, as the factory already tells failing from refusing for its other effects.
- It tries again only while the step's context lasts and its watcher may act for it, and it checks the lease before each try, as it does before every push.
- A refusal, a ref that moved to anything else, or a lost lease ends it at once, as now.

`Record` should do the same for a run's record. Today, a push that landed despite GitHub's error returns `ErrRecorded`, as if another watcher had recorded the step, and the run then looks stopped before it ever started. Instead:

- After a failed push, a ref that holds the record's own commit means the push landed, and `Record` succeeds. The nonce makes every record its own commit.
- A ref holding any other record is `ErrRecorded`, as now.
- GitHub failing is tried again, on the same terms as `Finish`.

The tests should show:

- `Finish` succeeds when a push failed with a 5xx but landed.
- `Finish` succeeds after one or more 5xx failures followed by a success.
- `Finish` stops at once on a refusal, on a ref that moved elsewhere, and when the watcher loses the lease or the context ends.
- `Finish` gives up after its last wait with the last error.
- The waits stay within the step's context.
- `Record` succeeds when a failed push landed its own commit.
- `Record` still returns `ErrRecorded` for another watcher's record.
- `Record` tries GitHub failing again on the same terms as `Finish`.

`docs/factory.md`'s recovery section and the matching line in `SPEC.md` must say this.
title: Record a run's result through GitHub's push failures

## Summary
In BA full-auto mode on Claude Code cloud (strata-kb 1.34.3), a `ba-ticket-author` task finished `done` and its PR merged, but kb-publish skipped the ticket because its Definition of Ready was 7/8. The loop has no step that comes back to finish the ticket. Because it picks from the session branch, it reads the story as `to-draft`, waits on it 5 times and then skips it. The story never reaches `ready` on the hub without a manual fix.

Seen on `vuonglq01685/myflix-ba`, story `M-catalog-discovery-US4`.

## What happened
1. `ba-ticket-author:M-catalog-discovery-US4` drafted the ticket and also settled a new technology decision, D52, which moved the mission to rev 23. Both went into the same PR (`vuonglq01685/myflix-ba#217`), which merged. The task ended `done` after 1409 s.
2. In the task, `kb_ticket_check` read the parent mission from the hub's published plan, which was still at rev 22 and had no D52. It reported 11 lines of `decision D52 not in mission`. The task could not pass the local mission as `mission_markdown` because the file is about 220 KB, too large for the MCP call. It correctly left the last DoR box ("Technical grounding … kb ticket check PASS") unticked.
3. kb-publish published mission rev 23 (`vuonglq01685/myflix-center-kb#246`) but skipped the ticket:
   ```
   skipped: tickets/M-catalog-discovery/M-catalog-discovery-US4.md — Definition of Ready not fully ticked (7/8)
   ```
4. The runner then logged, every `idle_interval`:
   ```
   ba-ticket-author:M-catalog-discovery-US4 ended done but is still picked; waiting for the hub
   ```
   After `MAX_SAME_PICK` (5) of these, `_repicked` would move the story to `skipped`.
5. Re-running `kb_ticket_check` after the publish gave `Grounding: PASS`. A manual one-line PR that ticks the box is the only fix today (`vuonglq01685/myflix-ba#218`).

## Root causes
1. **`done` does not mean ready.** `runner.py` treats `TaskResult("done")` (`claude.py:46`) as finished as soon as the PR merges. It does not check whether the ticket's DoR is complete, which is what `planingest.py:217` uses to decide whether the ticket gets published.
2. **A decision and its ticket cannot pass in one task.** When the ticket cites a `[NEW: D<n>]` decided in the same task, the hub cannot see D<n> until that PR is published. On cloud the local mission cannot be passed instead when it is large. The grounding box is then always left unticked.
3. **No task re-checks after publish.** `picker._ba_tasks` yields only: mission blocker → `--amend` for `draft` stories → `next` → `to-draft`. Nothing re-runs `kb ticket check` and ticks DoR once the hub has caught up.
4. **On cloud the picker reads the session branch, not `origin/<default>`.** `picker._mission_next` runs `kb mission next --json` in `root`. On cloud `root` is the session branch, which does not get the merged ticket, because the PR merged into `main`. So the story reads as `to-draft`, when on `main` it would be `draft`. That gives the same task key as `last_done` and triggers `_repicked` (wait, then skip). If it had read `draft`, `ba-ticket-author --amend` would have been picked, and that would likely have fixed it.

## Suggested fixes
- When the picker reads plan state, use `origin/<default_branch>` (already fetched in preflight, `runner.py:81`), or a worktree of it, not the working tree of `root`.
- After a `ba-ticket-author` task ends `done`, check the merged ticket's DoR. If it is incomplete, queue a follow-up task (re-run `kb ticket check` and tick DoR, or `--amend`) for after the publish, instead of waiting on `same_pick` and skipping.
- Let `kb_ticket_check` take the parent mission when the file is too large for one MCP call. For example, it could take only the mission's `## Technology decisions` table, or read the mission from a ref of the BA repo.
- When a story is skipped, log the reason the hub gave (e.g. `DoR 7/8`) so the skip can be traced without digging into the kb-publish logs.

## Environment
- strata-kb 1.34.3 (CI pin 1.34.0), repo kind `ba`, `cloud: true`, `idle_interval: 600`
- Code read at `5e98773`: `src/strata_kb/autorun/picker.py` (`_mission_next`, `_ba_tasks`), `src/strata_kb/autorun/runner.py` (`_repicked`, `MAX_SAME_PICK = 5`)
title: kb auto (BA, cloud): ticket ends `done` with DoR 7/8, is never re-checked, and gets skipped

`cargo jackioh spec fold` or its pull request failed on main at ec882eeb6ecbc86189664aacbd884dd98e7f50ce ([the run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41087760341)), so `spec/pending/` stays as it is and `spec/INDEX.md` is not rewritten.

The run's log names the failure (`spec check` rule 6 refuses a pending file the fold cannot place). Fix it on a branch whose `cargo jackioh spec check` passes; once it merges, run this workflow again (Actions -> spec fold -> Run workflow) or wait for tomorrow's run.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41097414467)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

**Human required:** in Actions, open the failed spec fold run, [41087760341](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41087760341) (`gh run view 41087760341 --log-failed`), and find the step that failed. Every file a bot may change is already correct, and the failure is in a step a bot can neither see nor edit (checkout, setup, or "open the fold pull request" in `.github/workflows/spec-fold.yml`). Fix that cause by Step 2 or Step 3 below, then run the workflow again (Actions → spec fold → Run workflow).

## Goal

Get the daily fold working again. `cargo jackioh spec fold` runs on `main`, its pull request opens and merges itself, `spec/pending/` is emptied into `spec/11-rulings.md`, and `spec/INDEX.md` is rewritten. Then #2528 is closed.

What I checked on this branch's base, 8a0b772f7 (`git diff --stat ec882eeb6 HEAD -- spec` is empty, so `spec/` is the same as at the failing commit):

- **The issue's hint does not apply.** All 23 files that `git ls-tree --name-only ec882eeb6 spec/pending/` lists are `<digits>.md` and none is empty. So `spec check` rule 6 (`pending_problems` in `crates/tools/src/spec.rs`) cannot have failed there. The issue text is the workflow's fixed template, not the log.
- **`spec check` passes:** `target/release/jackioh spec check` printed `spec check: 1533 rulings, 3561 proofs, 47617 citations in 2996 files, 18832 links: ok`.
- **The fold itself works:** `jackioh spec --root <copy> fold` on a `git archive HEAD` copy printed `spec fold: 23 pending paragraph(s) into spec/11-rulings.md (#2127, …, #2499)` and `spec index: wrote spec/INDEX.md (1533 rulings)`, exit 0. `spec check` on the folded copy passed too.
- **The token and auto-merge work:** `patches-ship.yml` uses the same `BOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `gh pr create` and `gh pr merge --auto --squash`, and its pull requests kept merging through the merge queue on 2026-10-30 (#2523, #2527).

## Files to touch

| Path | new/change | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/spec-fold.yml` | change, only if the log shows Step 2's cause | The `branch=` line of the step "open the fold pull request" |

Nothing else. The fold's code (`crates/tools/src/spec.rs`: `fold`, `read_pending`, `pending_problems`) and `spec/` itself (`spec/pending/*.md`, `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md`) are correct. They must not be hand-edited, and no branch runs `cargo jackioh spec index` (CLAUDE.md rule 3; `spec/README.md`, "Adding a ruling"). No bot may make the workflow edit (CLAUDE.md, "The night bot"). No ruling or spec section is involved.

## Steps

1. **Read the log.** Open run 41087760341 and note the failing step and its last error lines.

2. **If the step "open the fold pull request" failed at `git push`** (rejected, non-fast-forward, or the branch already exists), the cause is a second run on the same `main` commit. The branch name `patches/spec-fold-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)` is the same for every run on one commit. `main` stayed at ec882eeb6 from 15:47Z to 16:27Z, so a run there finds the first run's branch, and its own commit differs (a new timestamp), so the push is refused.
   - In `.github/workflows/spec-fold.yml`, in that step, replace
     `branch="patches/spec-fold-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"`
     with
     `branch="patches/spec-fold-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)-$GITHUB_RUN_ID"`.
   - The supersede loop still matches the new name (`startswith("patches/spec-fold-")`) and skips its own branch, so the newer run closes the older pull request.
   - `vercel.json` skips `patches/` branches by prefix (the workflow's header says so), so the longer name changes nothing there.
   - Make it a pull request of its own. The `bot selftest` check covers workflow files.

3. **If the step failed at `gh pr close`**, an older fold pull request was still open. It may have been in the merge queue, or conflicting with #2474 (9c9bcbd99, 14:34Z), which edited `spec/INDEX.md` and `spec/11-rulings.md` after the 09:37Z run.
   - Close that pull request and delete its `patches/spec-fold-*` branch by hand.
   - **Otherwise**, if the failure was transient (a network or cache error in checkout or setup), there is nothing to change.

4. **If the step "fold" failed after all,** with a message naming a file, comment the error on #2528 and take the `human required` label off, so a bot can fix that file with the real error in hand. My checks above say this should not happen on today's `main`.

5. **Run it again.** Actions → spec fold → Run workflow, on `main` (`gh workflow run spec-fold.yml`). `main` has moved past ec882eeb6, so the branch name is new even without Step 2's edit.

6. **Wait for the pull request** "Patch: fold the pending §11 paragraphs and the rulings index into the spec" to merge itself. Then close #2528.

## Tests

No Rust or web test changes; the fold already has unit tests in `crates/tools/src/spec.rs`:
- `folds_the_pending_paragraphs_in_number_order_and_rewrites_the_index`
- `check_holds_the_pending_paragraphs_to_their_names_and_never_the_index_to_the_notes`

Run them with `cargo test -p jackioh-tools spec::tests`.

To prove the fold on today's `main` without touching the checkout:

```
cargo build --release -p jackioh-tools
rm -rf /tmp/fold && mkdir /tmp/fold && git archive HEAD | tar -x -C /tmp/fold
"${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-target}"/release/jackioh spec --root /tmp/fold fold
"${CARGO_TARGET_DIR:-target}"/release/jackioh spec --root /tmp/fold check
```

Both must exit 0. The real proof is Step 5's run going green and its pull request merging.

## Done when

## Hypothesis

**We think that** a revision asked to "bring this branch up to date with main" can report success while nothing reaches the branch. On PR #3096 (`work-3073`) the worker reported three times — 29 Oct, 4 Nov 10:15 and 10:36 UTC — that the branch "already contains current `origin/main`" ("confirmed against the remote tip"), yet on 4 Nov 11:00 UTC GitHub's compare shows `work-3073` **406 commits behind** `main` (`compare/main...work-3073`: behind 406, ahead 1) and the PR stays conflicting. The same runs also refused to push with "⚠️ Not pushed — this PR changed while I was working", although the PR's head had not changed (PR #3096 comments 10:15 and 10:37 UTC). PR #3096 has had the owner's `ok` and a build-review go since 29 Oct / 3 Nov and cannot merge.

**We'll do that by** making a revision prove its result instead of asserting it: after the base merge and push, read the branch back from GitHub and check that it contains the base tip (`compare/<base>...<branch>` `behind_by == 0`); if not, fail on the PR with the actual numbers. And find why the "PR changed while I was working" guard fires when the head is unchanged.

**We'll be right if** a "bring up to date" run either leaves the branch with `behind_by == 0` on GitHub, or fails visibly on the PR saying how far behind it still is — never "done" while behind.

**We'll know by** PR #3096: the next merge-main run ends with `behind 0`, or with a failure naming why.

## 👤 For humans

When you ask the pipeline to bring a PR up to date, it checks on GitHub that it really is, and tells you on the PR if it isn't — no more "done" while nothing happened.

- Reproduce first from the run logs for #3096 (runs around 10:15 and 10:36 UTC on 4 Nov): which ref did the worker compare against? The checkout fetches `origin/main` with `--depth=1` at a fixed SHA — check whether "already contains" was judged against that shallow ref or the wrong branch, and whether the base-merge commit was ever pushed.

- Add the post-push check (`behind_by` via the compare API) to the revise path and to the #2941 "brought up to date" step; a nonzero result fails the run with a PR comment carrying the numbers.
- Tests: compare result behind 0 → done; behind > 0 → fail with numbers; head unchanged → no "PR changed" refusal.

After this change the practice menu also offers "today's deal": one fixed shuffle per day that every player gets, so friends can compare how they did with the same cards, and a shared replay file proves what happened. ## Why - The design pillars are seeded randomness, chaos and short sharp games (`spec/01-overview.md` §1): a date-derived seed is the cheapest possible shared ritual, and the deck streams already exist (`{seed}:human-deck`, `{seed}:ai-deck` in `crates/server/src/economy/practice.rs`'s header; R433 dealt decks). - It needs no server, no account and no leaderboard: the client deals from the date seed under the current catalog, and the existing replay download (R1141000, `apps/web/src/replay/download.ts`) is already the verifiable, name-free way to share a result. - This is new: rejected #1998 (hand-built one-turn puzzles) and #1193 (trap minimums in dealt decks) are different ideas, and no open issue covers a shared daily setup. ## Proposal - Add a "Today's deal" entry to the practice setup (`apps/web/src/practice/PracticeSetup.tsx`) that starts an All Random game from a `daily-` seed with the player's usual difficulty and lean choices; the seed rolls over at UTC midnight. - Reuse the practice worker path (`core.ts`) unchanged, including earning claims (the seed is a normal practice seed) and the catalog-version check on saves. - Document it as a practice setup option in the spec's practice section (§9.9), not as a mode: queue, ranked and records are untouched. ## Where it lands - `apps/web/src/practice/` (`PracticeSetup.tsx`, `core.ts`, `protocol.ts`); `spec/09-architecture.md` §9.9 (one paragraph); no engine, server or catalog change. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] Two devices starting today's deal get identical human and AI decks and identical AI behavior. - [ ] Yesterday's deal is still replayable from its seed; today's changes at UTC midnight. - [ ] A finished daily game claims earning exactly like a normal practice game, and its downloaded replay opens in the replay player. - [ ] A catalog patch does not silently re-deal mid-day games under new cards (the save/version rule decides, and says so). ## Size and risks Small-medium: web client plus a spec paragraph; The `decks` match within a day, and today's do not equal yesterday's. - `it("R2882000 two devices playing today's deal get the same AI moves", { timeout: 120_000 }, …)`: - this copies core.test.ts's B38 option, so no existing timeout is raised; - two `playOn(dailyDealConfig(TODAY, "medium", null), REQUESTS)`; - `log` and `hash` are equal; - `first.log.filter((a) => a.nonce.startsWith("a")).length` is greater than 1. - **`apps/web/src/practice/earning.test.ts`**: `it("R2882000 today's deal asks for no seed: it plays its day's own")` checks that `seedRequestOf(config({ seed: "daily-2026-11-03", dailyDeal: "2026-11-03" }))` is null. - **`apps/web/src/practice/controller.test.ts`**, in the R508 describe after the R1303003 test: `it("R2882000 today's deal starts with no last board, so every device deals it alike")`. - Call `writeLastBoard([{ defId: "core-008", radiant: false }])` and set `config = { ...CONFIG, dailyDeal: "2026-11-03" }`. - `void controller.start(config); await flush();` - The last request body equals `{ type: "start", config }`. - **`apps/web/src/practice/resume.test.ts`**: `it("R2882000 today's deal is kept as one, and a day that is not a string is malformed")`. - Write `{ ...CONFIG, dailyDeal: "2026-11-03" }` and read it back equal. - `CONFIG` reads back with no `dailyDeal`. - Stored `{ ...CONFIG, dailyDeal: 3 }` reads as null. - **`apps/web/src/routes/practice.test.tsx`**: inside `describe("R1303000 earning…")`, after "an anonymous player, a URL seed and a lesson ask for nothing", add two tests. Each one: - starts with `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["Date"] }); vi.setSystemTime(Date.parse("2026-11-03T12:00:00.000Z"));`; - uses `renderEarning(host, earning)` with `fakeEarning()`; - ends with `requestSeed` never called. `it("R2882000 Play today's deal starts the UTC day's deal at the setup's difficulty and pick: no server seed, no sandbox, no last board")`: - Call `writeLastBoard([...])` (import from `../practice/lastBoard.ts`), then `await settle({ ticks: 10 })`. - Click `T.medium`. - Set the deck to `random` and the `practiceTestid.leanNewest` picker to `"Classic+"`. - Set the deck to `preset:humans` and tick `practiceTestid.sandbox`. - Click `practiceTestid.dailyDeal`, then `await screen.findByTestId(T.hud)`. - `host.starts()[0]` toEqual `{ seed: "daily-2026-11-03", difficulty: "medium", humanSeat: "p1", deck: { kind: "random", leanSet: "Classic+" }, dailyDeal: "2026-11-03" }`. - `PRACTICE_SETUP_KEY` holds `{ difficulty: "medium", deck: "preset:humans", leanSet: "Classic+" }`. `it("R2882000 Play again on today's deal deals the day's deal at the click, the new day's after UTC midnight")`: - Start the deal as above. - Call `concedeOnBoard()` and wait for `T.result`. - `vi.setSystemTime(Date.parse("2026-11-04T00:00:01.000Z"))`, then click `T.playAgain`. - Wait for two starts. `starts()[1]` toMatchObject `{ seed: "daily-2026-11-04", humanSeat: "p2", difficulty: , deck: , dailyDeal: "2026-11-04" }`. Commands: - `sh scripts/build-wasm.sh` - `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/practice/todaysDeal.test.ts src/practice/earning.test.ts src/practice/controller.test.ts src/practice/resume.test.ts src/routes/practice.test.tsx src/i18n/i18n.test.ts src/writing.test.ts` - `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` - `pnpm exec eslint apps/web` - `cargo jackioh spec check` **Done when.** - [ ] Play today's deal starts the UTC day's deal (seed, seat, random deck with the setup's difficulty and pick), with no server seed and no last board. - [ ] Two cores deal and play today's deal the same way; yesterday's deals the same way again and differs from today's; the deal rolls over at UTC midnight. - [ ] Play again and a reload keep a game as today's deal. - [ ] The §9.9 paragraph, `R2882000.md` and `pending/2882.md` are written, and `spec check` passes. - [ ] Every test above passes. So do `typecheck`, `eslint`, the i18n and writing tests, `cargo fmt --check`, and the harness's checks. `git status` shows none of the "must not touch" files changed. **Risks.** - **Losing the deal to a server seed.** If `seedRequestOf` is not changed (step 4), an active account's daily deal gets the server's seed instead. The route tests prove the step. - **Determinism.** A last board from the device (R508), a random seat or a different catalog would split the deal between devices. Steps 3 and 5 keep the first two out, and §9.9 names the catalog. A slow device whose AI hits `PRACTICE_AI_CLOCK_MS` may decide differently; §9.9 says so, and core.ts is left as it is. - **Hidden information.** Nothing new crosses the worker boundary. `dailyDeal` travels from page to worker inside the config, as `earning` does. - **Replay.** Saves and kept games carry the config unchanged; `resumeGame` still refuses a save from another catalog (criterion 4). - **Copy.** Write the new strings exactly as given, with their zh-CN entries, or `i18n.test.ts` and `writing.test.ts` fail. - **Test time.** The play test makes real AI decisions. Keep `REQUESTS` at 30 and the B38 timeout option; never raise any other timeout. **Open questions.** - **Earning (criterion 3).** The issue assumes the daily seed is "a normal practice seed". It is not: the server issues each account's earning seed and stores it as a primary key, so this plan makes today's deal earn nothing and says so on the setup. Earning on it would take a server-issued daily seed for each account, which deals from a shared deal seed, plus a migration. That is a hard, cross-crate follow-up issue only a person can approve. - **Seat rule.** The seat goes by the parity of the day of the month (odd: p1, even: p2), so two odd days fall in a row at a month's end. A person may prefer always p1 or another rule.

**Labels:** `architecture`, `bot:build`, `bot:fullsend`, `difficulty:hard`, `priority:low`. It is a fullsend: one part per area below, reconciled into one pull request. **No logic changes**: nothing a test, a replay, a player or another service can observe may change.

## Why

#598 (parts #599 to #603) cut the comments by about 2 MB on 2026-10-09. The tree has since doubled, and so have the comments. Measured at `0e5ae82` (2026-10-30):

| What | Then (`9ad2612`) | Now (`0e5ae82`) |
|---|---|---|
| Tracked files | 3,466 | 7,373 |
| Rust and TypeScript source | 22.7 MB | 48.1 MB |
| Whole-line comments in that source | 6.56 MB | **10.20 MB, about 2.5 M tokens, 21% of the source** |
| Banner rule lines (`// ----…`, `// ====…`) | — | 2,058 |

Every agent that opens a file pays for its comments. Most of the weight is still history that belongs in `git log` or `docs/v0.3.0/`, banner rules, comments that restate the next line, and paragraphs that retell a ruling `spec/rulings/` already holds.

## Scope: three kinds of change, nothing else

1. **Comments** (the main lever): compact whole-line comments by the rules below.
2. **Stale files**: delete dead files and archives by `.github/hygiene/files.md`'s rules, sections 1 and 2, word for word (its look-dead-but-are-not list included). If the weekly hygiene issue is open when this runs, leave its dead files to it and do only what it has not claimed.
3. **Long local names** (minor: there is little to win, about 3 Rust `let`s and 120 TypeScript locals of 25 characters or more): shorten a function-local name only where the shorter one is as clear in its scope.

**Out of scope:** dead code and duplicated logic (the code audit's, `.github/hygiene/code.md`), any edit to a code line other than a local rename, markdown rewording, and every path the checker refuses (generated files, files tests read as text, the doc comments ts-rs exports, the spec, `BUILD.md`, `REVIEW.md`, the agent instructions, the designer's source notes, the catalog, the patch JSON, the golden traces, migrations, and the bots' `forbidden_paths` and `review_paths`).

## Parts (a suggested split: no file in two parts)

| Part | Paths | Source files | Comment bytes now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `crates/engine` (src and tests) | 574 | 2.78 MB |
| 2 | `crates/cards` (scripts and tests) | 836 | 2.31 MB |
| 3 | `crates/server` | 234 | 1.74 MB |
| 4 | `crates/ai`, `crates/tools`, `crates/luau`, `crates/wasm` | 233 | 0.97 MB |
| 5 | `apps/web/src/game/` | 209 | 0.50 MB |
| 6 | the rest of `apps/web` | 1,075 | 1.66 MB |
| 7 | `e2e` | 95 | 0.23 MB |
| 8 | stale files and archives (deletions only, any path the checker allows) | — | — |

Each of parts 1 to 7 does its own comments and its own renames. Part 8 edits no file except to drop a citation of a file it deletes, and only in a whole-line comment.

## Comment rules

Edit **only whole-line comments**: a line whose first characters are `//`, `///`, `//!`, `/*` or `/**`, and the lines inside a `/* … */` block. Work through each file top to bottom.

**Delete:**
1. **Port history.** A sentence about the TypeScript version (`TS`, `ports.ts`, `packages/…`, `apps/server/…`, `← \`path\``, "as TS stored them", `PORT-MAP`). If it also states a rule or reason that still holds, keep that part.
2. **Change history.** "used to", "previously", "formerly", "no longer", "renamed from", old version numbers. A card's number (`C+ #29`) is not history: keep it.
3. **Restating the code.** A comment that only says what the next line plainly does.
4. **Banner rules.** `// ----…` and `// ====…` lines. Keep the title between two rules, so three lines become one.
5. **Commented-out code.**

**Shorten** a block of more than 4 lines left after that: keep the **why** (the constraint, the invariant, the ordering trap, the ruling), say it once, cut walk-throughs and examples a test already shows. Aim for 4 lines a block, 12 for a `//!` header. Prefer deleting whole lines to rewording them.

**Always keep:**
- **Every cite**, at least once in the file: `R123`, `R1365000`, `§9.4`, `CLAUDE.md rule 7`, audit ids like `B36`, and issue numbers like `#902` (this codebase uses them as design pointers: "#442 L8", "#902 V4"). The checker fails when one vanishes from a file.
- **Directives**: `// eslint-disable…`, `// @ts-…`, `// prettier-ignore`, `// rustfmt::skip`, `// SAFETY:`, `#[allow]` reasons, every `TODO` and `FIXME`.
- **Fenced blocks** (` ``` `) in doc comments, byte for byte: Rust runs them.
- A `//` line inside a string, raw string or template literal: that is data.
- Cross-file contracts ("must equal `render.yaml`'s …", "keep in step with …") and the header comment every card script has (CLAUDE.md rule 6).
- **Anything you cannot tell carries no reason.** A smaller diff beats a wrong deletion.

## Rename rules

- Only a Rust `let` binding, closure parameter or match binding, or a TypeScript `const`/`let`/parameter that is not exported, inside a function body. Never a `pub` or exported item, a field, a variant, a prop, a type, a test's name (rule 3's `r58` tokens), a `#[serde]`/ts-rs/`#[no_mangle]`/Luau-kit name, or a name another file, doc or comment names (`git grep -nw <name>` first).
- No rename inside a multi-line string, raw string or template literal: the checker cannot see those lines as strings.
- Rename in a commit of its own within the part, so the reconcile's review reads it apart from the comment edits.

## How to check (each part, then the reconcile)

Save the script at the bottom to `/tmp/compact_check.py` (**never commit it**) and run it from the repository root against the base the part started from (the integration branch's base for a part, `origin/main` for the reconcile):

```
cargo fmt
python3 -I /tmp/compact_check.py <base> --renames
cargo fmt --check
cargo jackioh spec check
```

It must print `OK`. `CODE CHANGED`: a line other than a whole-line comment differs beyond a rename; put it back. `CITE LOST`: put the cite back into a comment that stays. `FENCE CHANGED`: restore the fence. `NOT ALLOWED`: revert that file. A deleted file is listed, never failed: the pull request's table must prove it.

The reconcile also runs, and every one must leave `git status` clean:

```
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --features jackioh-engine/testkit,jackioh-engine/ts   # rewrites apps/web/src/wire/: it must not
cargo test -p jackioh-luau --features ts --test export_api                     # rewrites jackioh.luau: it must not
cargo jackioh golden check
cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims                             # kind internal, no card plays differently
pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck && pnpm --dir apps/web test && pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e
```

## Done when

- [ ] `python3 -I /tmp/compact_check.py origin/main --renames` prints `OK` on the reconciled branch; its output is in the pull request.
- [ ] `git ls-files '*.rs' '*.ts' '*.tsx' | xargs grep -hE '^\s*(//|/\*|\*)' | wc -c` is at least **2,500,000 bytes** below `0e5ae82`'s 10,203,957 (the pull request gives the figure, and each part's).
- [ ] `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` labels it `kind:internal` with no card that plays differently and no pending fragment; no ruling is added; no generated file changes.
- [ ] The five required checks (`rust`, `web`, `e2e smoke`, `db`, `bot selftest`) are green on the pull request's head (CLAUDE.md rule 12).
- [ ] The pull request body has: a table of every deleted file (path, size, the commands that show nothing reads it, as `files.md` asks); the list of renamed files; and what was left alone and why.
- [ ] Nothing under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/` or `.claude/` changes; anything worth trimming there is named in the pull request for a person.

## The checker (`/tmp/compact_check.py`)

Tested at `0e5ae82` in a scratch worktree: a clean tree, comment-only edits, local renames and file deletions print `OK`; a code or string-literal edit prints `CODE CHANGED` and `FAIL`.

<details>
<summary>Show the script</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Usage: python3 -I compact_check.py [base-ref] [--renames]   (default origin/main). Run from the repo root.
Proves a token-compaction change left the logic alone. Every changed .rs/.ts/.tsx file must differ only in
whole-line comments (with --renames: or in identifiers alone, every string literal byte for byte), keep each
cite it had, and leave doc-test fences alone. A deleted file is listed for the pull request's table. Exits 1
on any failure."""
import fnmatch, json, re, subprocess, sys
from collections import Counter

args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
base = args[0] if args else "origin/main"
RENAMES = "--renames" in sys.argv
SRC = (".rs", ".ts", ".tsx")
# Never edited: generated files, files tests read as text, and doc comments ts-rs exports into TypeScript.
EXTRA = ("apps/web/src/wire/", "apps/web/src/wasm/pkg/", "crates/cards/luau/jackioh.luau",
         "crates/engine/src/wire/", "crates/engine/src/config.rs", "crates/engine/src/state.rs",
         "crates/engine/src/validator.rs", "crates/server/src/config.rs", "crates/server/src/env.rs",
         "crates/server/src/cli/seed_accounts.rs", "apps/web/src/routes/privacy.tsx",
         "crates/server/migrations/", "crates/engine/tests/golden/", "crates/cards/catalog.json",
         "crates/cards/patches/", "spec/", "SPEC.md", "BUILD.md", "REVIEW.md", "CLAUDE.md", "AGENTS.md",
         "GEMINI.md", "JackiOh_*.md", "ARCHITECTURE-CCG.md", "docs/*-set.md", "docs/classic-sets.md")


def matches(path, patterns):
    """The night bot's path rule (bot/harness/git.py): `dir/` is a directory from the repo root, a pattern
    with `/` is a glob on the whole path, a bare name is a glob on the last part."""
    path = path.lower().removeprefix("./"); name = path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    for raw in patterns:
        pat = raw.lower().removeprefix("./")
        if pat.endswith("/"):
            if path == pat.rstrip("/") or path.startswith(pat): return True
        elif "/" in pat:
            if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(path, pat): return True
        elif fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pat): return True
    return False


_cfg = json.load(open(".harness/config.json"))
NEVER = _cfg["review_paths"] + _cfg["forbidden_paths"] + list(EXTRA)
CITE = re.compile(r"\bR\d+\b|§\s?\d+(?:\.\d+)*|CLAUDE\.md rule \d+|\bB\d{1,3}\b|#\d{2,5}\b")
IDENT = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
STR = {".rs": re.compile(r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"'),
       ".ts": re.compile(r'"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|\'(?:\\.|[^\'\\])*\'|`(?:\\.|[^`\\])*`')}
STR[".tsx"] = STR[".ts"]


def sh(*a):
    return subprocess.run(a, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout


def split(text):
    """(code lines, comment lines): a line whose first token is // or /* (to the closing */) is a comment."""
    code, com, inb = [], [], False
    for l in text.split("\n"):
        s = l.strip()
        if inb:
            com.append(l); inb = "*/" not in s
        elif s.startswith("//"):
            com.append(l)
        elif s.startswith("/*"):
            com.append(l); inb = "*/" not in s
        elif s:
            code.append(l.strip())  # blank lines and indentation are the formatter's
    return code, com


def fenced(com):
    out, on = [], False
    for l in com:
        if "```" in l:
            on = not on; out.append(l.strip())
        elif on:
            out.append(l.strip())
    return out


def shape(lines, ext):
    """The code with every string literal set aside and every identifier blanked: equal shapes and equal
    strings mean only names changed."""
    strs, out = [], []
    for l in lines:
        strs += STR[ext].findall(l)
        out.append(IDENT.sub("I", STR[ext].sub("S", l)))
    return out, strs


bad, deleted, renamed, b_old, b_new = 0, [], [], 0, 0
status = [l.split("\t") for l in sh("git", "diff", "--name-status", "--no-renames", base).splitlines()]
for st, p in status:
    if matches(p, NEVER):
        print(f"NOT ALLOWED  {p}: generated, read as text, a source note or the spec"); bad += 1; continue
    if st == "D":
        deleted.append((p, len(sh("git", "show", f"{base}:{p}").encode()))); continue
    if st != "M" or not p.endswith(SRC):
        print(f"NOT ALLOWED  {p}: only edits to .rs/.ts/.tsx files and deletions"); bad += 1; continue
    new, old = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read(), sh("git", "show", f"{base}:{p}")
    (oc, ocm), (nc, ncm) = split(old), split(new)
    if oc != nc:
        ext = "." + p.rsplit(".", 1)[1]
        if RENAMES and shape(oc, ext) == shape(nc, ext):
            renamed.append(p)
        else:
            print(f"CODE CHANGED {p}: lines other than whole-line comments differ"
                  + ("" if RENAMES else " (a rename part runs with --renames)")); bad += 1
    oq, nq = Counter(CITE.findall("\n".join(ocm))), Counter(CITE.findall("\n".join(ncm)))
    lost = sorted(c for c in oq if c not in nq)
    if lost:
        print(f"CITE LOST    {p}: {lost} (each cite must survive once in a comment that stays)"); bad += 1
    if fenced(ocm) != fenced(ncm):
        print(f"FENCE CHANGED {p}: a ``` block inside a comment was edited"); bad += 1
    b_old += sum(len(l.encode()) + 1 for l in ocm); b_new += sum(len(l.encode()) + 1 for l in ncm)
for p, size in deleted:
    print(f"deleted      {p} ({size} B): its row in the pull request's table says why nothing reads it")
for p in renamed:
    print(f"renamed      {p}: identifiers only")
print(f"{len(status)} files ({len(deleted)} deleted, {len(renamed)} with renames); comment bytes "
      f"{b_old} -> {b_new} ({100 * (b_old - b_new) / max(b_old, 1):.0f}% less); "
      f"deleted bytes {sum(s for _, s in deleted)}")
print("FAIL" if bad else "OK")
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)
```

</details>
